newsitem.title: USA: Energy independents see growth through drillbit.
newsitem.headline: Energy independents see growth through drillbit.

text.p: Oil and gas independents smashed earnings records in the first quarter of 1997 but in an era of weaker commodity prices, growth is going to have to come from the drillbit and lower costs.

Anadarko Petroleum Corp, which reported revenues up 26 percent at $170.5 million and net income up 68 percent at $34.4 million aims to grow production by 17 percent this year and double it by 2000 based on three key fields in Algeria, its Mahogany and Agate fields in the Gulf of Mexico and onshore properties.

"Now, what is not in the forecast are any new discoveries in the next four years. We plan to spend over $100 million a year on exploration and we expect to make discoveries and if we do, we will beat this forecast," chief executive Robert Allison told the company's annual meeting on Thursday.
The company produced 23,000 barrels of oil per day in the first quarter from 19,000 a year ago and natural gas to 470 million cubic feet per day from 480 million.
The virtuous circle was completed with a 17 percent rise in crude oil prices to $20.58 per barrel and a 36 percent rise in natural gas prices to $2.66 per thousand feet.
Houston-based Santa Fe Energy Resources had the same experience as development in Argentina, the Gulf of Mexico and southeast New Mexico came on and crude oil prices rallied to $20.64 from $16.69.
A 10 percent rise in production at the company to 29,000 barrels a day combined with the price rise to push revenues up to $89.0 million.

At Fort Worth-based Cross Timbers Oil Co revenues rose 48 percent to $53.5million and earnings per share doubled to $0.40 per share as production rose 34 percent to 125.2 million cubic feet of natural gas a day and oil production rose eight percent to 10,359 million barrels.
First quarter gas prices rose 42 percent to $2.62 per thousand cubic feet and oil 14 percent to $21.36.
The company has a $70 million development budget this year, up from $40 million in 1996.
"Higher output will offset some of the effect of lower prices and we will be increasing production quarter on quarter," Louis Baldwin, the company's chief financial officer told Reuters.
Cross Timbers is also going to grow by buying properties, but Baldwin warned that if you wanted to buy good properties, you had to pay for them.
"You do not grow a company just by acquisitions, you have to improve what you buy," he said.
"Production and reserve growth is continuing and we are looking at an excellent inventory of drilling prospects, both offshore and onshore. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
